Native engineering interfaces — current development source

ForgeMCP retains its five foundation inspection tools and adds seventeen native engineering tools plus one local API retrieval tool. Inspect session identity and the project/scene first. All engineering calls require an explicit session ID. Natural language is interpreted by the MCP client (Codex or another authorized agent), which constructs the typed recipe; the application adapters contain no model/provider logic.

Gameplay Ability System inspection and setup

unreal_inspect_gas(actor_path, session_id) reads GAS state from one exact actor in the current idle editor world. It returns bounded AbilitySystemComponent identity, replication mode, owner/avatar identity, initialized actor-info state, finite base and current attribute values, owned tags, granted ability classes/levels/input IDs/active state, and active GameplayEffect classes/levels/stacks/durations. Component, attribute, tag, ability, and effect arrays include counts and truncation flags. It does not activate abilities, apply effects, or change the actor.

New Blueprint recipes can add a replicated AbilitySystemComponent with an explicit minimal, mixed, or full effect-replication mode. Minimal and mixed modes require a matching ForgeMCP startup component. Unreal does not serialize the base ASC replication-mode field into Blueprint component templates, so ForgeMCP stores that requested mode in the startup component's typed Blueprint properties. It applies the mode when the component registers and again before startup configuration at BeginPlay. Blueprint inspection reports the configured mode separately from the ASC template default. The startup component can also name AttributeSet, ability, and GameplayEffect classes and applies those gameplay changes on the authoritative actor at BeginPlay. This is a starting-configuration path, not full GAS authoring: creating/editing GameplayAbility, AttributeSet or GameplayEffect assets, tag requirements, cues, network behavior and gameplay execution remain incomplete and need project-specific acceptance.

Unreal Blueprint construction

unreal_class_info returns native reflected property types and Blueprint-callable function signatures. recipe_supported identifies functions currently permitted in graph recipes. Inspection is broader than executable recipe capabilities.

unreal_preview_blueprint validates a new /Game package path, a concrete native actor parent, unique variables/components/functions, node IDs and graph references. It returns an expiring session-local preview ID and the reviewed changes. No existing asset can be overwritten. unreal_apply_blueprint requires confirmation equal to that ID and a user task authorizing the exact changes. A preview is consumed once.

Recipes can add primitive variables, native actor components, void functions, overridden parent events, custom events, variable get/set nodes and approved native function calls. Branch, Sequence, Self and Reroute are also supported. Sequence execution_outputs accepts 2–16 and creates then_0, then_1, etc. Other node kinds use the default value of two without additional execution pins. Native schema links propagate reroute types. Boolean pin defaults accept true/false/0/1; invalid defaults discard the scratch Blueprint rather than silently retaining a different value. Pin defaults and connections use native graph schemas. Apply compiles the Blueprint and returns compiler errors/warnings, diagnostics, graph/pin inspection, operation state and affected paths. save and place are explicit flags, both false by default. location uses Unreal centimeters. Placement does not save the level.

Pin/compile failures discard the newly created scratch asset before any save. Requested save/placement failures report partial; inspect saved, placed, and diagnostics. A successful transport response is not proof that the operation state is completed. unreal_inspect_blueprint returns variables, components, graphs, node IDs, pin types/defaults/links, compilation status and truncation indicators.

The current function set covers approved actor transforms/visibility, pure native math/string functions, and PrintString/PrintText/IsValid. It excludes arbitrary Python, console execution, and editor scripting escape routes. Broader existing Blueprint editing, arbitrary node families, component property assignment, GAS and UMG are still being developed. This version does not expose every Unreal operation.

Blender scene recipes

blender_inspect_object returns transforms, mesh counts, materials, modifiers, collections and Action identity. blender_inspect_rig reads an explicit armature's bone hierarchy and related meshes; optional skin-weight summaries are capped at 256 bones, 32 related meshes, 100000 total vertices, and 2 million vertex-group assignments per query. blender_preview_scene accepts 1–32 typed operations:

  • create_mesh: bounded vertices/faces, optional collection and transforms.
  • set_vertices: matching vertex-count edits; copies existing mesh data first.
  • set_transform: location, Euler rotation in radians, and nonzero scale.
  • create_material / assign_material: RGBA base color and mesh material assignment.
  • create_collection: adds a new collection to the active scene.
  • keyframe: location, rotation_euler or scale at an explicit frame.
  • bone_keyframe: location, Euler rotation, normalized quaternion rotation, or scale keyframes on an exact pose bone in an armature. Euler/quaternion mode must match the bone's current rotation mode; scale components cannot be zero.
  • scene_settings: FPS, frame start and frame end.
  • set_material_input: bounded numeric/vector/RGBA input defaults on approved native nodes in an existing local material; preview reports shared object users.
  • duplicate_object: new named copy of a local mesh/empty, with independent mesh and Action data; optional destination collection and local transforms. Mesh duplication is bounded at 100000 vertices. Source geometry/animation changes invalidate previews.

Apply requires the reviewed preview ID as confirmation. It rechecks the scene fingerprint and rejects stale or replayed plans. Existing mesh and Action datablocks are preserved through copies before editing. Failed batches restore object and pose-bone state, material defaults, and scene timing and remove only newly created datablocks; rollback failures report partial. Results name preserved datablocks. The tool does not save a .blend file. There is no raw Python execution endpoint. Large mesh transfer, rig construction and weight editing, modifiers, existing material graph editing, and export/import remain in development.

Shader graph creation and inspection

create_material can provide shader_nodes (at most 32) and shader_links (at most 64). Graphs are built only on a newly created material. Node IDs are unique identifiers; each custom graph has exactly one material output. Links name their source/target node and socket identifier or unique socket label. Repeated socket labels require identifiers, which the inspector returns. Cycles, duplicate targets and nonallowlisted node types are rejected. Structural checks happen at preview; native socket/type/default validation happens during apply and any failure invokes whole-batch rollback.

The native node allowlist contains Material Output, Principled BSDF, RGB, Value, Math, Mix RGB, Noise Texture, Texture Coordinate, Mapping, Bump, Vector Math, Separate XYZ and Combine XYZ. Numeric input defaults are bounded and dimensions must match native sockets. RGB and Value nodes accept outputs defaults for their native constant sockets, so constants can feed color/scalar graph connections. Other node types cannot set output defaults. Math/vector/blend operations use explicit allowlists. Script nodes, external file inputs and arbitrary properties are absent. Existing material input defaults can be edited; adding/removing existing nodes and links remains unsupported.

blender_inspect_material returns node types/IDs/positions, input/output socket identifiers/types/defaults, link endpoints/validity and material identity. It caps inspection at 64 nodes, 32 sockets per direction per node, and 128 links, with counts and truncation flags. Apply returns the resulting new material graph inspection.

Unreal Asset Registry queries

unreal_search_assets queries native registry metadata on the editor game thread. It accepts a content directory (default /Game), an exact native /Script/ class filter, case-insensitive name substring, recursive path flag, limit (1–200) and offset (0–100000). Results are sorted by object path and report total count, next offset, truncation and registry-loading state. Changes to the live registry between pages can shift results. Registry loading can make any query incomplete.

unreal_inspect_asset accepts a package path or object path and returns registry metadata, at most 64 tags (values capped at 512 characters), and bounded package dependencies and referencers. These are registry package references, not live UObject references or editable property values. Neither command loads, compiles, saves or changes assets. Native requests reject unknown fields and require exact JSON types.

Unreal actor recipes

unreal_inspect_actor resolves an exact actor path in the loaded editor world and returns GUID, class, label, world transform and game-hidden state. It does not expose arbitrary editable UObject properties. unreal_preview_actors accepts 1–32 operations; unreal_apply_actors consumes its session-local ten-minute preview with matching confirmation. It rejects changed target/world state and editor PIE contexts.

  • spawn: native StaticMeshActor, PointLight, SpotLight, DirectionalLight or CameraActor, with optional label, world transform and game-hidden state.
  • transform: changes an exact existing actor path's location, rotation and/or scale.
  • visibility: changes hidden (game-hidden state, not editor viewport visibility).

Location uses centimeters, rotation is [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees, and scale must be nonzero. Existing actor edits require a root component and no attach parent. Native transactions support editor undo. Failed batches restore recorded transforms and hidden state and remove newly spawned actors; rollback status is explicit. No level is saved and no deletion, arbitrary class execution or generic property setter is exposed. Rollback of values does not promise to reverse external side effects of an existing actor's editor callbacks. Inspect returned state and actor facts.

Version-aware API retrieval

forge_search_api_docs(application, version, query, limit) retrieves local reference chunks for an exact major.minor.patch version. It uses SQLite FTS5 lexical retrieval for client-side RAG, without cloud APIs or embeddings. Unreal indexing reads the installed official Python stub as text and never imports it. Blender export reads RNA and Python API reference metadata in a separate factory-startup process. Source text is reference data, never an instruction or permission to execute code.

& '[local path] --background --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python "$PWD\scripts\blender_export_api_docs.py" -- "$PWD\Saved\Knowledge\blender-5.2.2.jsonl"
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\index_api_docs.py --unreal-engine '[local path] Files\EpicGames\UE_5.6' --blender-jsonl Saved\Knowledge\blender-5.2.2.jsonl

The index is project-local under Saved/Knowledge, excluded from Git and plugin ZIPs. Wrong-version searches return no results; there is no silent version fallback. An API appearing in documentation does not grant an adapter capability. Verify actual native support before constructing a recipe. Generated references retain upstream ownership.

Recovery and validation

Requests remain bounded at 16 KiB. Split overly large tasks into supported operations; there is no silent truncation of mutations. Apply exchanges allow 60 seconds; a timeout reports outcome_unknown. Inspect before retrying because the preview may be consumed and the application may have completed the change. Inspection exchanges remain 10 sec.

Native tests use isolated projects and factory scenes. Run verify_blender_recipes.py in background factory Blender, and verify_engineering_live.py only with its guarded Saved/Milestone2/HostProject sessions. Evidence and current gaps are recorded in Development_Status.md. No visual panel click-through or gameplay execution claim follows merely from successful compilation and placement.

Existing Blueprint graph edits

unreal_preview_blueprint_edits and unreal_apply_blueprint_edits edit an existing, successfully compiled normal /Game Blueprint in an idle editor. Recipes can add bounded primitive variables and native ActorComponents, plus allowlisted event, custom event, variable get/set, branch, sequence, self, reroute and native function nodes, then wire those nodes by temporary recipe IDs. Operations can also move approved existing nodes, set validated input defaults, and connect/disconnect inspected pins. Results return native node GUIDs for follow-up edits. The tools do not add/delete existing variables, components, functions or arbitrary node families.

Preview records graph state, compilation status, dirty state and editor identity; changes to that recorded state invalidate apply. It does not fingerprint every Blueprint property or component default. Apply requires the one-use matching preview confirmation, writes a bounded Blueprint-state recovery journal under the project Saved directory, performs a native transaction, and compiles the result. Failed batches restore recorded graph state and recompile; recovery failures report partial. Schema-generated conversion nodes are removed during recovery. The journal is not a full binary asset backup. Existing asset files are never saved by these edit tools. Interactive editor Undo and runtime Blueprint behavior require separate validation.

Existing Blender material input edits report shared object users before apply and restore input defaults after a failed batch. Material graph inspection and the edited socket values participate in preview staleness checks; not every shader property is fingerprinted. No material render or saved-file acceptance is implied.
